o.norm: Consonants from the same code group separated by W or H are treated as one. @throws EncoderException for some failure scenarios

i.norm:
Verifies the H/W rule: after the first character, H and W are completely silent and do not act as separators between consonants. This means that inserting H or W between two letters does not change the resulting Soundex code, regardless of whether those letters share the same code group.

Example pair: "Sgler" and "Swhgler" both encode to "S460" because the inserted 'wh' is silently skipped.

The rule also explains why many differently-spelled surnames (SAILOR, SCHILLER, SHULER, etc.) all collapse to the same Soundex code S460.

@throws EncoderException for some failure scenarios
Baseline encoding without any H or W between consonants
Inserting 'wh' between the same consonants still yields S460, proving that H and W are silently ignored after the first character
Real-world surname spellings that all map to S460 via the H/W rule and other Soundex collapsing rules (vowels, duplicate codes, etc.)
